page: Microsoft Azure E128ds_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor. The instance provides 128 dedicated vCPUs across 64 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, backed by a substantial 480 MB L3 cache. It features 1024 GB of system memory, maintaining an 8 GB per vCPU allocation ratio, alongside 7559 GB of bundled high-speed local NVMe SSD storage. Hardware acceleration extensions include AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX).

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional multi-threaded computational capabilities and throughput. While single-core performance on stress-ng falls in the average tier at 2282.07, parallel processing scales to 144593.74, placing it in the top decile. Memory bandwidth is notable, reaching 655.3 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 253.51 GB/sec for writes. Database processing metrics reflect these strengths, achieving top-tier status in PassMark database operations (33918.49) and Redis SET operations reaching 209.67 million operations per second. Multi-threaded decompression and compression tests also score in the top tier.

Without discrete GPUs, LLM execution relies entirely on host compute and AMX instruction support. Small to large model prompt ingestion rates place in the top 25%, while autoregressive text generation speeds remain moderate. The combination of large memory capacity, dedicated high core count, and fast local NVMe storage provides high density for demanding enterprise workloads without requiring multi-node distributed setups.

Microsoft Azure E128ds_v7 is tailored for large-scale in-memory databases, distributed caching layers such as Redis, enterprise relational databases, large-scale data transformation (ETL) pipelines, and memory-intensive analytics.

Supported by AVX-512 and AMX instruction sets, it delivers strong performance across data manipulation and matrix operations. The instance is suited for enterprise relational and in-memory database systems, large-scale Redis deployments, data analytics, and high-throughput memory-bound processing.
